severity_definitions.high: Wrong or unsafe core conclusion under stated valid conditions; blocks reuse.
severity_definitions.medium: Material factual, semantic or example error affecting the taught method.
severity_definitions.low: Bounded helper robustness/coverage, navigation, reproducibility or editorial improvement; normal worked example remains valid.

findings.title: H07 M2 bypasses the conflict guard used by M1
findings.evidence: first_completed selects the first encountered lowest revision without validating duplicate business contents. Two B:r1 inputs differing only in cents yield 8000 or 8100 as input order changes; current_completed rejects the same pair. See probes-results.json IR-01.
findings.impact: The alternate metric silently weakens the revision-identity rule while the lesson changes only which completion to count. This is a small synthetic-helper inconsistency on invalid/conflicting input, not a failure of the shown 30000-cent example.
findings.repair: Factor revision-content validation ahead of both metric selectors, or explicitly require and demonstrate a shared validated-input stage. Preserve the complete M1/M2 explanation.
findings.acceptance_check: Both input permutations reject/quarantine a conflicting same revision; equal-content redelivery with a different received time remains harmless; M1=20000 and M2=30000 remain unchanged.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: H08 conflicting event identity has no explicit policy
findings.evidence: deduplicate uses setdefault. Same tenant/connection/event with severity 40 then 99 yields score 40; reverse the order and it yields 99. Equal-content replay correctly leaves one signal.
findings.impact: A reader can reuse first-wins deduplication without deciding how evidence collisions are handled. The chapter names source identity and raw-digest references, but does not explicitly promise collision quarantine; this is an omitted precondition/robustness lesson, not a demonstrated provider or live security defect.
findings.repair: Specify immutable-content requirements and quarantine conflicting same-key input, or require verified immutable upstream events before this helper. Keep normalization version distinct from event identity.
findings.acceptance_check: Identical replay stays one signal; conflicting contents block trusted scoring in either order, or fail a documented upstream validator.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: X01 eligibility accepts values outside the boolean domain
findings.evidence: record coerces eligible with int(), and the schema has no eligible IN (0,1) constraint. For 400 units, eligible=2 gives 800 billable and 1.6 amount; eligible=-1 gives -400 and -0.8.
findings.impact: The helper can manufacture negative or excess billable units from malformed eligibility. All supplied boolean fixtures still pass; no exposed production ingestion endpoint is present.
findings.repair: Validate the eligibility domain at ingestion and add a matching SQLite check. State the accepted usage numeric type and rounding policy separately; INTEGER affinity alone does not enforce integer inputs.
findings.acceptance_check: True/False or explicitly permitted 0/1 retain outputs; 2, -1, malformed strings and null are rejected without a persisted charge.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: H04 rehire test demonstrates desired state, not stale-task delivery
findings.evidence: The test computes desired(27)/desired(32), assigns historical_e1_revoke=False and asserts it differs from desired(32). It never delivers E1 after E2, calls an apply/dispatch handler, or observes target state.
findings.impact: This test cannot catch a stale-task handler that deactivates the rehired account. Its comment explicitly limits it to desired-state modeling; the chapter correctly lists delivery-order behavior as a future check. The gap is coverage clarity, not evidence of an implemented unsafe SCIM connector.
findings.repair: Rename/report this as a desired-state counterexample; add a small revision-aware fake dispatch/reconciliation exercise if stale-task safety is to be presented as executed.
findings.acceptance_check: Deliver E2 enable then E1 revoke (and reverse order), check final current-authorized state, and show a naive handler failing. Unknown external effects remain unresolved until reconciled.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: Five references have empty destinations
findings.evidence: These lines contain respectively ‘这个模型是本例的设计约束，见 。’, ‘这个演算与修订政策见 。’, ‘这个补充是原创分析，见 。’, and ‘设计政策见 。’. The empty phrase is visible in the published chapter text and does not link to evidence or a local definition. The chapter link scan independently found these four blanks; H08 had no corresponding blank (one regex match there was ordinary prose, not a broken reference). H06:28 additionally ends with “合成模型与关闭 guard 对应 。” and likewise has no destination.
findings.impact: Readers reach an incomplete “见 。” or “对应 。” reference instead of the intended model or policy explanation. Existing case/evidence footer links still work.
findings.repair: Restore the specific local link, or remove the dangling phrase when the design is already explained in place. Do not send the reader to re-audit a whole source ledger.
findings.acceptance_check: Read H07:22,82,96, X01:5 and H06:28 after rendering; every reference either reaches its intended explanation or is removed.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: FHIR citations mix explicit R5 and moving release URLs
findings.evidence: The same paragraph uses /R5/ for Observation but moving /fhir/ links for ServiceRequest and DiagnosticReport. The primary R5 ServiceRequest page supports the scoped request/result distinction.
findings.impact: No incorrect resource meaning was established. The mixed citation boundary makes the checked release less reproducible.
findings.repair: Pin all resources in the paragraph to the intended release, or label intentional mixed versions and their limitations in the evidence record.
findings.acceptance_check: Reopen the three chosen release pages and retain resource-specific locators.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: Authoring residue and malformed citation punctuation remain in prose
findings.evidence: V15:73 ends with an imperative authoring fragment “记录这组原创演算。”; V16:78 appends a broken scope-note fragment. V01/V02/V03, V06, V07, V19 and V21 contain orphan enumeration punctuation around citations.
findings.impact: The process fragments interrupt the teaching voice. These are local copyedits, not reasons to compress or remove full worked explanations.
findings.repair: Delete the authoring instruction; integrate or remove the already-redundant synthetic note; repair separators/spacing while preserving source links, numbers, qualifications and explanations.
findings.acceptance_check: Read the exact locations as connected prose and render links; no domain meaning changes.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes

findings.title: Room-range exclusion option omits its scalar GiST prerequisite
findings.evidence: The sample proposes an exclusion constraint over hotel_id, room_id, and daterange to block same-room overlap. PostgreSQL's range documentation confirms range exclusion and explains that combining scalar equality with a range exclusion may require the btree_gist extension (or an appropriate operator class). Without this prerequisite, the DDL implied by the example may not be available for ordinary scalar room identifiers.
findings.impact: A reader implementing this optional stack choice may not have an equality operator class for ordinary hotel/room IDs. No failing DDL was published or executed, and a locking alternative is already given.
findings.repair: Mention btree_gist or appropriate operator classes if implementing scalar equality plus range overlap. Keep the locking alternative.
findings.acceptance_check: If a runnable DDL example is added, create it on the stated PostgreSQL version and verify same-room overlaps reject while distinct rooms and adjacent dates pass.
findings.status: open; review only, no content changes
